title: September 2025 spend and cost per click by channel

brief.decision: Which paid channels to look at first in next month's channel plan, from September 2025 spend, clicks and cost per click in the monthly performance report
brief.deadline: The monthly performance report, due tomorrow

expected_output.grain: one row per paid channel, including a paid channel with no spend in September 2025

checkpoints.prompt: Aoife needs one cost per click for each paid channel for September 2025. Mailvora's spend data has one row per campaign and day, with that day's spend and clicks, and a channel runs several campaigns. How should a channel's September cost per click be worked out?

options.text: Add up the channel's September spend over all its campaigns and days, then divide it by its September clicks added up the same way
Work out a cost per click for each campaign and day, then take the average of those daily figures over the month
Work out each campaign's cost per click for the month, then take the average of those campaign figures across all the campaigns in the channel
Divide the channel's September spend by the number of signups it brought in during September

checkpoints.prompt: Aoife's report needs the total number of clicks behind the September 2025 cost per click. Add up the clicks of every paid campaign on every UTC day of spend from 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-30, both days included. Type a whole number.
Write the query that answers Aoife's question.

Aoife's headline is the paid channel whose clicks cost the most in September 2025. A channel's cost per click is the spend of all its campaigns on the UTC days from 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-30, both days included, divided by the clicks of those campaigns on the same days; a channel with no clicks in that period has no cost per click. What is the highest cost per click of any paid channel? Type the amount in euros, rounded to 2 decimals.

In Aoife's September 2025 table, brand search has the lowest cost per click of the paid channels and LinkedIn the highest. Nothing else has been checked yet. Aoife asks: is brand search our most efficient channel?

options.text: Yes. Its clicks cost the least, so every euro spent there buys the most visits, and visits are what the paid channels are paid to bring in.
Not from this table. A cost per click says nothing about what a click is worth, and brand search mostly reaches people already looking for Mailvora.
No. LinkedIn is the most efficient channel, because the high price of its clicks shows that LinkedIn visitors are worth more to Mailvora than visitors from any other channel.
Yes, as long as its average daily cost per click over the month is also the lowest, which rules out one cheap week making it look better than it is.

checkpoints.prompt: Write 2 to 4 sentences for Aoife's monthly report: which paid channel's clicks cost the most in September 2025 and what that does and does not tell us, one caveat, and one next step.

model_plan:
Metric formula: spend_eur is the channel's September 2025 spend and clicks its September clicks, both added up over its campaigns and days; cpc_eur = spend_eur divided by clicks, rounded to 2 decimals, and missing when clicks is 0.
Output grain: one row per paid channel (every channel outside the unpaid group), whether or not it spent in September.
Tables and keys: ad_spend_daily joins campaigns on campaign_id, which gives each campaign's channel_id; channels is kept whole with a LEFT JOIN on channel_id.
Filters: spend_date from 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-30, both days included (UTC days); channels whose channel_group is not unpaid.
Edge cases: a paid channel with no September spend keeps its row with 0 spend and 0 clicks; a channel with spend and no clicks gets a missing cpc_eur, not 0 and not a division by 0; the cost per click is total spend over total clicks, not an average of daily figures; a month number without its year would add September 2024.
Expected row count: 7
model_answer_template: LinkedIn's clicks cost the most of any paid channel in September 2025, at {CP4} euros a click, while brand search had the cheapest clicks. A cost per click prices traffic, not results: LinkedIn may bring fewer but better signups, and brand search mostly reaches people who were already looking for Mailvora. Before ranking channels by efficiency, I would add each channel's signups, paid conversions and revenue to this table and compare the cost per signup and the return on spend.
follow_up_question: Which of our paid channels is the most efficient?
